name: NiveshTrade
tagline: A discount stock broker where 09:15 is the moment of truth
summary: NiveshTrade serves 40 lakh investors: live prices, charts, order placement, risk checks, exchange connectivity, holdings, funds and alerts. Every trading day opens at 09:15 with a burst of orders, and on Budget day the Finance Minister's speech moves the whole market. Frozen prices, orders stuck in 'pending' and slow margin checks keep coming back.

tour.headline: The exchange gateway has no circuit breaker or failover line, so every line drop leaves orders stuck in 'pending'; fixing it costs 14 hours.

incidents.title: Live prices froze for 3 minutes at market open
incidents.desc: At 09:15 the price feed stopped updating for every user until 09:18; investors traded on stale prices.
whys: Prices stopped updating at 09:15
The tick fan-out loop fell behind when subscriptions jumped at the open
One process fans out every tick to every socket in a single loop
incidents.lesson: The open is the one moment the feed must not stall.

incidents.title: Login and two-factor failing for 6 minutes before the opening bell
incidents.desc: From 09:12 to 09:18 most logins failed; the app retried every failed login immediately.
whys: Investors could not log in before 09:15
The app retried failed logins instantly and multiplied the traffic
Login has no rate limiting or backoff, so app retries become a storm
incidents.fix: Scaled the login service up for the morning.
incidents.lesson: Retries without backoff turn a blip into an outage.

incidents.title: Orders took 8 seconds to be accepted at 09:15
incidents.desc: Order acceptance slowed from 200 ms to 8 seconds in the first five minutes of trading.
whys: Order acceptance slowed to 8 seconds
Every order's margin check queried holdings and ledger balances
The RMS check reads holdings and margins from the database for every order
incidents.lesson: Every order paying for the same reads does not scale.

incidents.title: Charts take 20 seconds to load for 5-year ranges
incidents.desc: Long-range charts loaded slowly or timed out for popular stocks.
whys: Long-range charts were very slow
Candle queries scanned the whole candles table
Candle tables have no index on symbol and time

incidents.title: Orders stuck in 'pending' when the primary exchange line dropped
incidents.desc: The primary leased line to the exchange dropped at 11:02 and orders stayed pending for 11 minutes.
whys: Orders were not confirmed for 11 minutes
Every order kept retrying the dead primary line
The exchange gateway has no circuit breaker or failover to the backup line
incidents.fix: Switched to the backup line by hand.
incidents.lesson: Eleven minutes of pending orders on a volatile day is a disaster.

incidents.title: Order executed after the investor cancelled it
incidents.desc: An investor cancelled a limit order; the fill arrived at the same moment and both updates were applied.
whys: A cancelled order was executed
The cancel and fill updates were applied out of order
Order updates are applied without row-level locking or version checks
incidents.fix: Reversed the trade with the investor's consent.
incidents.lesson: Order state needs a single, ordered writer.

incidents.title: Same buy order placed twice after the app retried
incidents.desc: Investors on slow networks got two identical buy orders; the app retried after 3 seconds and the OMS accepted both.
whys: Investors got two identical orders
The app retried after a slow response and both orders were accepted
Orders are accepted without a client order ID to detect repeats
incidents.fix: Cancelled the duplicates and compensated losses.
incidents.lesson: Any retry can double an order.

incidents.title: UPI fund additions not reflected in trading balance
incidents.desc: Money added by UPI between 09:00 and 09:20 did not appear in the trading balance for 2 hours.
whys: Money added by UPI did not show up
The bank's confirmation callback was lost
Fund additions are never reconciled with the bank statement
incidents.fix: Credited the balances from the bank's file.
incidents.lesson: We relied on a callback that can be lost.

incidents.title: Holdings page shows yesterday's quantities after 15:30
incidents.desc: During the contract-note run, holdings and positions showed stale quantities for 40 minutes.
whys: Holdings were stale after 15:30
Portfolio queries waited for database connections
Back-office batch jobs share the trading database pool during market hours
incidents.lesson: The batch still runs while trading systems need the database.

incidents.title: Price feed lagged 90 seconds on results day
incidents.desc: When a large company announced results, subscriptions tripled and prices lagged by 90 seconds.
whys: Prices lagged by 90 seconds
The fan-out loop could not keep up with the surge in subscriptions
One process fans out every tick to every socket in a single loop
incidents.fix: Moved half the users to a second feed process.
incidents.lesson: Splitting users by hand is not a design.

incidents.title: Two-factor login storm at 09:14 locks out investors
incidents.desc: Login requests tripled at 09:14 as apps retried failures instantly; many investors were locked out.
whys: Logins failed just before the open
Apps retried instantly and overwhelmed the login service
Login has no rate limiting or backoff, so app retries become a storm
incidents.fix: Released an app update that waits 1 second before retrying.
incidents.lesson: Old app versions still retry instantly.

incidents.title: Margin checks slow at open; orders rejected with a timeout
incidents.desc: Orders were rejected with 'RMS timeout' between 09:15 and 09:21 on expiry day.
whys: Orders were rejected at 09:15
Margin checks took over 5 seconds each
The RMS check reads holdings and margins from the database for every order
incidents.lesson: A longer limit only delays the rejection.

incidents.title: Wrong margin blocked after the peak-margin circular
incidents.desc: After a margin rule change, intraday orders were blocked with excess margin for one day.
whys: Investors were blocked with excess margin
The new margin percentage was updated in only one code path
Margin rules are hard-coded in the RMS code
incidents.lesson: Regulator rules change; code releases should not be needed.

incidents.title: Orders pending for 7 minutes during an exchange line flap
incidents.desc: The primary exchange line flapped for 7 minutes and orders hung in pending until it stabilised.
whys: Orders stayed pending
Order routing kept waiting on the failing primary line
The exchange gateway has no circuit breaker or failover to the backup line
incidents.fix: Waited for the line to recover.
incidents.lesson: The backup line sat idle the whole time.

incidents.title: Order execution alerts arriving 10 minutes late
incidents.desc: Push and SMS alerts for executed orders were delayed by up to 10 minutes at the open.
whys: Alerts were late
Alerts are sent inline by the order service and were dropped under load
Order alerts are sent synchronously without a queue
incidents.lesson: Alerts should never slow the order path.

incidents.title: Duplicate sell orders after a slow network response
incidents.desc: An investor sold twice the intended quantity when the app retried a sell order on a slow mobile network.
whys: An investor sold twice the intended quantity
The retried order was accepted as a new order
Orders are accepted without a client order ID to detect repeats
incidents.lesson: The same bug, a costlier day.

incidents.title: Funds added this morning not available for trading
incidents.desc: UPI additions made before 09:15 are missing from trading balances; investors cannot buy.
whys: Fund additions are missing
Bank callbacks failed and nothing re-checked them
Fund additions are never reconciled with the bank statement

incidents.title: Orders rejected with 'pool exhausted' at 15:20
incidents.desc: In the last 10 minutes of trading, order placement failed for 6 minutes while the contract-note job ran early.
whys: Orders failed in the last 10 minutes of trading
The contract-note job held most database connections
Back-office batch jobs share the trading database pool during market hours
incidents.lesson: Back office and trading must not share connections.

incidents.title: Live prices frozen for 2 minutes after the open
incidents.desc: Prices froze again at 09:15 this morning; the feed caught up at 09:17.
whys: Prices stopped updating at the open
The fan-out loop could not keep up with new subscriptions
One process fans out every tick to every socket in a single loop

incidents.title: Orders stuck in pending again during a line failure
incidents.desc: The primary exchange line failed at 10:40 and orders have been pending for 9 minutes.
whys: Orders are stuck in pending
Routing keeps retrying the failed primary line
The exchange gateway has no circuit breaker or failover to the backup line

debts.title: Fan out ticks through a message queue to socket workers
debts.desc: Publish each tick once to a message queue and let a pool of socket workers push it to subscribers, so the open cannot stall one loop.
debts.cause: One process fans out every tick to every socket in a single loop

debts.title: Serve RMS checks from cached holdings and margins
debts.desc: Keep each account's holdings, limits and ledger balance cached in memory, updated on every fill and fund change, so a margin check never reads the database.
debts.cause: The RMS check reads holdings and margins from the database for every order

debts.title: Circuit breaker with failover to the backup exchange line
debts.desc: Open a circuit breaker when the primary line fails and fail over to the backup line within seconds; close it again when the primary recovers.
debts.cause: The exchange gateway has no circuit breaker or failover to the backup line

debts.title: Client order IDs to make order placement idempotent
debts.desc: Every order carries a client order ID; a repeat with the same ID returns the first order instead of creating a new one.
debts.cause: Orders are accepted without a client order ID to detect repeats

debts.title: Row-level locks and a version column on order updates
debts.desc: Apply cancel, modify and fill updates under a row lock with a version check so they cannot be applied out of order.
debts.cause: Order updates are applied without row-level locking or version checks

debts.title: Reconcile UPI fund additions with the bank every 10 minutes
debts.desc: Match every UPI and net-banking credit in the bank statement with a fund addition and credit any that were missed.
debts.cause: Fund additions are never reconciled with the bank statement

debts.title: Rate limits and exponential backoff for login retries
debts.desc: Server-side rate limits per account and IP, and clients that back off with jitter after a failed login.
debts.cause: Login has no rate limiting or backoff, so app retries become a storm

debts.title: Separate connection pools for trading and back-office batch jobs
debts.desc: Give the contract-note and other back-office batch jobs their own small connection pool so they can never starve order placement.
debts.cause: Back-office batch jobs share the trading database pool during market hours

debts.title: Composite index on candles by symbol and time
debts.desc: Index the candles table on (symbol, timestamp) so long-range charts read only the rows they draw.
debts.cause: Candle tables have no index on symbol and time

debts.title: Send order alerts through a durable queue
debts.desc: The order service publishes alert events to a durable queue; a worker sends push, SMS and email.
debts.cause: Order alerts are sent synchronously without a queue

debts.title: Move margin rules into configuration
debts.desc: Margin percentages and peak-margin rules become configuration with an effective date, used by every code path.
debts.cause: Margin rules are hard-coded in the RMS code

debts.title: Load test the market open at 15x before Budget day
debts.desc: Replay a market open at 15 times normal order traffic against staging before Budget day and each monthly expiry.

debts.title: Paginate and archive trade history older than two years
debts.desc: Archive old trades to cold storage and paginate the trade-history API instead of returning every trade.

debts.title: Use the exchange holiday calendar for order validity
debts.desc: Good-till-date orders now expire using the exchange calendar in IST.

spike.name: Union Budget day
spike.description: The market opens at 09:15 and the Finance Minister's speech at 11:00 moves every stock: order traffic peaks at twelve times a normal day's open, and the closing half hour is busy again.

events.name: Credential-stuffing attack
events.description: From 02:00 a botnet tries leaked passwords against lakhs of accounts, thirty times a normal morning's logins, and keeps going into the 09:15 open.
